Publius of Malta
aka: Publius, the chief man of the island (prōtos tēs nēsou)
note: Named only in Acts 28:7. Christian tradition (Saint Publius) makes him Malta's first bishop; the fetched sources treat the Acts Publius and the canonized bishop of Athens of the same name as distinct persons. No independent contemporary source names him.

label: The shipwrecked party landed on the island called Malta (Melitē)
statement: The island on which the shipwrecked party had landed was called Malta - Greek Melitē (Melítē), Latin Melita.
note: A minority identification with Melita Illyrica (Meleda/Mljet in the Adriatic), first argued by Constantine Porphyrogenite (10th century) and later by the Dalmatian monk Padre Georgi, is dismissed by William Robertson Nicoll (per the fetched Wikipedia 'Acts 28' article).

label: Malta's inhabitants were non-Greek-speaking 'barbaroi' of Punic origin
statement: The islanders are called 'barbaroi' - the standard Greek term for non-Greek speakers - natives of Punic (Carthaginian) origin whose native language was Punic.

label: The islanders showed unusual kindness, kindling a fire for the shipwrecked party
statement: The islanders showed the shipwrecked party unusual kindness: they kindled a fire and received them all, because of the rain that was falling and because of the cold.

label: A viper fastened on Paul's hand as he laid sticks on the fire
statement: When Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a snake (Greek echidna, 'viper') came out because of the heat and fastened on his hand.

label: The islanders read the snakebite as Justice (Dikē) pursuing a murderer
statement: Seeing the creature hanging from Paul's hand, the islanders said to one another that the man was surely a murderer who, though he had escaped from the sea, yet Justice (hē dikē - the goddess/personification Dikē) had not allowed to live.

label: Paul shook off the viper and suffered no harm; the islanders called him a god
statement: Paul shook the creature into the fire and was not harmed; the islanders, expecting him to swell up or fall down dead, watched a long time, saw nothing bad happen, changed their minds and said he was a god.

label: Malta's chief officer bore the title 'first of the Maltese' (prōtos Melitaiōn)
statement: In the Roman period the chief officer of Malta bore the title 'first of the Maltese' - Greek prōtos Melitaiōn (πρῶτος Μελιταίων), Latin Primus Melitensium - the phrase behind Luke's 'chief man of the island' (prōtos tēs nēsou) for Publius.

label: Publius, the chief man of the island, received and entertained the party three days
statement: Publius, the chief man of the island, who had lands in the neighborhood, received the shipwrecked party and courteously entertained them for three days.

label: Publius's father lay sick of fever and dysentery
statement: The father of Publius lay sick of fever and dysentery.

label: Paul prayed, laid hands on Publius's father and healed him
statement: Paul entered in to Publius's father, prayed, laid his hands on him and healed him.

label: The rest of the island's sick came and were cured
statement: After Publius's father was healed, the rest who had diseases in the island came and were cured.

label: The islanders honored the party and provisioned the ship
statement: The islanders honored the party with many honors, and when they sailed put on board the things that were needed.

label: They wintered three months on Malta and sailed in a ship that had wintered there
statement: After three months on the island the party set sail in a ship of Alexandria which had wintered in the island.

label: Ships carried figurehead signs; this Alexandrian ship's sign was the Twin Brothers (Dioscuri)
statement: The Alexandrian ship's sign (parasēmon, figurehead) was 'the Twin Brothers' - the Dioscuri, Castor and Pollux, honored as the patron gods and deliverers of sailors.

label: The ship put in at Syracuse and stayed three days
statement: Touching at Syracuse, they stayed there three days.
note: Kind corrected from place to event in consolidation B: the statement is an event (the matrix anchors office/event/object/custom/time claims).

label: From Syracuse they arrived at Rhegium
statement: From Syracuse they circled around and arrived at Rhegium, at the Strait of Messina.
note: Kind corrected from place to event in consolidation B: the statement is an event (the matrix anchors office/event/object/custom/time claims).

label: With a south wind they came the second day to Puteoli
statement: After one day at Rhegium a south wind sprang up, and on the second day they came to Puteoli in the Bay of Naples.
note: Kind corrected from place to event in consolidation B: the statement is an event (the matrix anchors office/event/object/custom/time claims).

label: Jews lived in a community at Puteoli (Dicaearchia) before the Acts period
statement: There was a Jewish community at Puteoli (Dicaearchia), as at other Italian ports, before the events of Acts 28.

label: They found brothers at Puteoli and stayed seven days
statement: At Puteoli they found brothers and were entreated to stay with them seven days; so they came toward Rome.

label: Paul's party came to Rome
statement: After the seven days at Puteoli, the party came to Rome.

label: The Market of Appius (Appii Forum) was a staging halt on the Via Appia
statement: The Market of Appius (Appii Forum) was a post station on the Via Appia, about 43 Roman miles southeast of Rome, the usual halt at the end of the first day's journey from Rome.

label: The Three Taverns (Tres Tabernae) was a staging halt on the Via Appia
statement: The Three Taverns (Tres Tabernae) was a post station on the Via Appia, about 50 km (31 miles) from Rome, the last mansio before the city.

label: Roman brothers came out to meet Paul at the Market of Appius and the Three Taverns
statement: Brothers in Rome, hearing of the party, came to meet them as far as the Market of Appius and the Three Taverns; when Paul saw them he thanked God and took courage.

label: The centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard in Rome
statement: When they entered Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard (Greek stratopedarchēs).

label: Paul was held in military custody in private lodging under a guarding soldier
statement: Paul was allowed to stay by himself in private lodging with the soldier who guarded him - military custody (custodia militaris) of a prisoner awaiting trial, the 'chain' he mentions in 28:20 and the two-year arrangement of 28:30.

label: Rome had a settled Jewish community
statement: Rome had a settled Jewish community - large, long established, and with its own synagogues.

label: Diaspora Jewish communities had recognized lay leaders ('chief men')
statement: Diaspora Jewish communities of the period had recognized lay leaders - the 'chief men of the Jews' Paul summoned in Rome; Jewish community councils had titled heads (gerousiarchs) and officials.

label: Paul, examined and found guilty of nothing, had appealed to Caesar
statement: Paul told the Roman Jewish leaders that though he had done nothing against the people or the customs, he was delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into Roman hands, was examined and desired to be set free, and was constrained to appeal to Caesar; he was bound with a chain for the hope of Israel.

label: The Jewish leaders of Rome knew the Christian sect as 'everywhere spoken against'
statement: The Jewish leaders of Rome told Paul they had received no letters from Judea about him, but that concerning this sect it was known to them that everywhere it was spoken against.

label: Paul applied Isaiah 6:9-10 to his hearers, quoting it in full
statement: In his final Roman meeting Paul declared, 'The Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah, the prophet, to our fathers', and quoted Isaiah 6:9-10 in full against the divided hearers.

label: Paul stayed two whole years in his own rented house in Rome
statement: Paul stayed two whole years in his own rented house in Rome and received all who came to him.

label: Acts ends with Paul preaching 'with all boldness, without hindrance'
statement: Acts closes with Paul preaching the kingdom of God and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, without hindrance.

label: Paul later died a martyr's death in Rome under Nero (reception tradition)
statement: After the two Roman years Paul died a martyr's death in Rome under Nero - a tradition Acts does not record, reported first in reception texts (1 Clement 5; Eusebius, Ecclesiastical History 2.22).
note: Reception tradition, graded D: 1 Clement (c. 96) says Paul 'having borne his testimony... departed from the world' and, per Raymond Brown (fetched Wikipedia 'Paul the Apostle'), 'does not explicitly say' he was martyred in Rome; Eusebius (HE 2.22) places a second Roman ministry and martyrdom; the beheading detail is later still.

note: Jewish catacombs between the second and third miles of the Appian Way; epitaphs suggest at least eleven different Jewish communities in ancient Rome.

label: St. Paul's Catacombs, Rabat, Malta
note: 24 catacombs with Christian and Jewish burials side by side; a Jewish epitaph names Eulogia, wife of a gerousiarch (council head), herself a presbytera.

label: Malta's snake today: the European cat snake (Telescopus fallax)
date: first recorded in Malta 1894; recent studies treat it as native
method: species range records and herpetological studies
note: The European cat snake is venomous but rear-fanged, and its venom is not very effective against humans; no front-fanged viper (Viperidae) is recorded for Malta in the fetched sources.

label: Malta fever (Brucella melitensis) endemic in Maltese goats
date: 1887 CE (isolated by David Bruce); goat-milk transmission shown 1905 CE (Themistocles Zammit)
note: B. melitensis causes Malta fever (brucellosis) in humans, transmitted via goat milk; long endemic on Malta - a candidate background for the island's 'fever and dysentery'.

label: Malta's winter gregale: strong, cool northeasterly wind
note: The gregale is a Mediterranean wind that occurs when a low-pressure area moves south of Malta, bringing a strong, cool northeasterly wind to the island - the winter rain-and-cold context of Acts 28:2.

label: Acts 28:1
text: When we had escaped, then they learned that the island was called Malta.

label: Acts 28:2
text: The natives showed us uncommon kindness; for they kindled a fire, and received us all, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.

label: Acts 28:3
text: But when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat, and fastened on his hand.

label: Acts 28:4
text: When the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped from the sea, yet Justice has not allowed to live.”

label: Acts 28:5
text: However he shook off the creature into the fire, and wasn’t harmed.

label: Acts 28:6
text: But they expected that he would have swollen or fallen down dead suddenly, but when they watched for a long time and saw nothing bad happen to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.

label: Acts 28:7
text: Now in the neighborhood of that place were lands belonging to the chief man of the island, named Publius, who received us, and courteously entertained us for three days.

label: Acts 28:8
text: The father of Publius lay sick of fever and dysentery. Paul entered in to him, prayed, and laying his hands on him, healed him.

label: Acts 28:9
text: Then when this was done, the rest also who had diseases in the island came, and were cured.

label: Acts 28:10
text: They also honored us with many honors, and when we sailed, they put on board the things that we needed.

label: Acts 28:11
text: After three months, we set sail in a ship of Alexandria which had wintered in the island, whose sign was “The Twin Brothers.”

label: Acts 28:12
text: Touching at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.

label: Acts 28:13
text: From there we circled around and arrived at Rhegium. After one day, a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli,

label: Acts 28:14
text: where we found brothers, and were entreated to stay with them for seven days. So we came to Rome.

label: Acts 28:15
text: From there the brothers, when they heard of us, came to meet us as far as The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God, and took courage.

label: Acts 28:16
text: When we entered into Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard, but Paul was allowed to stay by himself with the soldier who guarded him.

label: Acts 28:17
text: After three days Paul called together those who were the leaders of the Jews. When they had come together, he said to them, “I, brothers, though I had done nothing against the people, or the customs of our fathers, still was delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans,

label: Acts 28:18
text: who, when they had examined me, desired to set me free, because there was no cause of death in me.

label: Acts 28:19
text: But when the Jews spoke against it, I was constrained to appeal to Caesar, not that I had anything about which to accuse my nation.

label: Acts 28:20
text: For this cause therefore I asked to see you and to speak with you. For because of the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.”

label: Acts 28:21
text: They said to him, “We neither received letters from Judea concerning you, nor did any of the brothers come here and report or speak any evil of you.

label: Acts 28:22
text: But we desire to hear from you what you think. For, as concerning this sect, it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against.”

label: Acts 28:23

label: Acts 28:24
text: Some believed the things which were spoken, and some disbelieved.

label: Acts 28:25
text: When they didn’t agree among themselves, they departed after Paul had spoken one word, “The Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah, the prophet, to our fathers,

label: Acts 28:26

saying,
